I just started reading The Doors of Perception by Aldous Huxley (who wrote Brave New World among many other things). Basically he decides to take mescalin as an experiment and then records his conversations with some "investigators" who are observing him. After he's come down he writes this short description of what happened while he was tripping. Aside from being a great read and making me wish I could meet Huxley, it was giving me psychedelic warm fuzzies. I've never done mescalin, but it reminded me of thoughts I've had while on acid. Has anyone done both and want to compare the two? Huxley says he isn't prone to visuals but I'm very prone to visuals. It also made me wonder whether the presence of the investigators and their prompting may have changed Huxley's trip and if that changes the way he was writing about it for audiences that probably had not taken psychedelics (at least at the time it was published).

Thoughts?

Also I just wanted to share this awesome piece with you guys.

Brave New World is extraordinary. When reading, keep in mind that it was written in 1931. I read Doors of Perception long after I read Brave New World. Find a local game shop and ask the clerk. Extremely high chance that they know the DnD groups or can get you in contact with someone that does.
